verdict: On unbranded prompts Skydo's USA page is the better-cited of the two: 86 citations from 90 fetches (0.96) against Infinity's 39 from 51 (0.76). The problem is different. In its top chat the page was cited six times and Skydo was not named: the facts it supplied (SWIFT details, ACH local details, FIRC and GST notes) were attributed to Wise, Payoneer and 'direct bank transfer' because Skydo's own method is labelled 'Virtual multicurrency accounts' and its facts sit in marketing blocks. And Skydo has one corridor; Infinity's page is the model for the six that are missing.

a.chat: Cheapest way to receive GBP in India (cited 4 times, position 2)
a.answer: Skydo: often very competitive for Indian freelancers and businesses receiving international payments, especially for invoices. It charges a flat fee instead of a percentage in many cases.
a.page: H2 3. Virtual GBP Account: 'platforms in India, like Infinity, Skydo, and Xflow, that allow Indian professionals to get a virtual GBP account with an account number and sort code'

a.answer: Direct SWIFT transfer to your Indian bank: convenient but often the most expensive due to exchange-rate markups and possible intermediary bank charges. PayPal: generally the most expensive because of high transaction fees and a significant exchange-rate markup.
a.page: H2 2. SWIFT > Limitations bullets; H2 5. PayPal > Limitations bullets

b.chat: how can i receive payments from my us client (cited 6 times, position 3; Skydo not named)
b.answer: Direct bank transfer (SWIFT): provide your client with your bank account number, SWIFT/BIC code, bank name and address. Often involves intermediary bank fees and less favorable exchange rates.
b.page: SWIFT card: Cons and Cost lines

b.answer: Your client can pay using local US bank details (ACH) if available (attributed to Wise). Payoneer gives you US receiving account details, allowing US clients to pay you via ACH.
b.page: H2 How your US client pays you via ACH: the mechanism is Skydo's but the page labels the method 'Virtual multicurrency accounts' and only says 'Skydo is one such option', so the credit went to Wise and Payoneer

b.answer: Issue an invoice for each payment. Keep the foreign remittance documentation (FIRC or eFIRC). If registered for GST, exports of services may qualify as zero-rated supplies.
b.page: FAQ answers on FIRA and 'safe and legal'

diagnosis: Corridor prompts are answered as a ranked list of methods for that corridor, each with a one-line cost verdict, then documents and tax. Skydo's USA page is cited well because its ACH/Fedwire and SWIFT facts fit that list; it loses the brand credit because those facts are not under Skydo's name.

The corridor-specific mechanism is the citation magnet: sort code and Faster Payments for GBP, ACH and Fedwire for USD. Skydo has the USD mechanism written well and gets no credit because the method heading is generic.

Name Skydo as the method. Infinity's page gets Skydo into a 'cheapest GBP' answer by listing 'Infinity, Skydo, and Xflow' under virtual GBP accounts. Skydo's own page says 'Skydo is one such option' after four marketing blocks.
A 'Your situation → best option' table is the decision block ChatGPT copies for corridor and persona prompts alike.
Thirty-nine CTAs. Six of them are between the six factors ChatGPT would otherwise quote as a list.
Documents and mistakes lists are cheap citations. Infinity has both; Skydo has neither outside the FAQ.
Skydo has no UK, EU, Canada, Australia or UAE corridor page in the window. Infinity has USD, EUR and GBP; 'send money from X to India' consumer guides fill the rest.
